authoredSolutions.1: The ball falls \(h=5\) m and rebounds to \(0.81h\) each time, so the coefficient of restitution is \(e=\sqrt{0.81}=0.9\). Total distance \(S=h\left(1+\frac{2e^{2}}{1-e^{2}}\right)\approx 47.6\) m and total time \(T=\sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}\left(1+\frac{2e}{1-e}\right)=19\) s, so the average speed \(=S/T\approx 2.5\ ms^{-1}\). Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.2: A non-linear polyatomic gas with 2 vibrational modes has \(f=3+3+2(2)=10\) degrees of freedom, so \(\gamma=\frac{C_p}{C_v}=1+\frac{2}{f}=1+\frac{2}{10}=1.2\). Hence option (B).
authoredSolutions.3: The amplitude of a damped oscillator decays as \(A=A_0 e^{-bt/2m}\). Solving for the damping constant \(b\) from the given amplitude drop after 120 s yields a value that does not match any of the listed options. Hence option (D), none of these.
authoredSolutions.4: Tracing the given combination of gates, the Boolean output simplifies to the expression shown in option (D). Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.5: The pressure at depth is \(P=h\rho g=2\times10^{3}\times10^{3}\times9.8\). The bulk modulus is \(B=\dfrac{P}{\Delta V/V}=\dfrac{1.96\times10^{7}}{1.36\times10^{-2}}\approx1.44\times10^{9}\ N\,m^{-2}\). Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.6: For a satellite \(T\propto R^{3/2}\). With the geostationary radius \(=12R\) (Earth-day 24 h) and the new orbit radius \(=3R\): \(\frac{24}{T}=\left(\frac{12R}{3R}\right)^{3/2}=8\Rightarrow T=3\) h. Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.7: Here \(\omega=2\pi f=2\pi(245)\approx1.5\times10^{3}\ rad\,s^{-1}\) and the amplitude is \(A=\frac{6}{2}=3\ cm=0.03\) m. These give the wave description in option (D). Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.8: Comparing the two thermodynamic processes on the \(P\)-\(V\) (or \(P\)-\(T\)) diagram, the correct relationship between the work done / heat exchanged is that of option (B). Hence option (B).
authoredSolutions.9: Since \(v=\frac{ds}{dt}=v_0+gt+Ft^{2}\), integrating from \(t=0\) to \(t=1\): \(s=\left[v_0 t+\frac{gt^{2}}{2}+\frac{Ft^{3}}{3}\right]_0^{1}=v_0+\frac{g}{2}+\frac{F}{3}\). Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.10: For an amplitude-modulated wave the bandwidth is \(2f_m\). With \(\omega_m=1.57\times10^{8}=2\pi f_m\), \(f_m=25\) MHz, so \(BW=2f_m=50\) MHz. Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.11: The series current is \(i=\frac{3E}{R+r_1+r_2}\). The terminal potential across the \(2E\) cell is zero: \(2E-ir_1=0\Rightarrow 2E=\frac{3E\,r_1}{R+r_1+r_2}\), which gives \(R=\frac{r_1}{2}-r_2\). Hence option (B).
authoredSolutions.12: The hairpin is two semi-infinite straight wires plus a semicircular loop: \(B=2\left(\frac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi r}\right)+\frac{\mu_0 i}{2r}\cdot\frac{1}{2}=\frac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi r}(2+\pi)\). Hence option (B).
authoredSolutions.13: Applying Kirchhoff's laws (node equations) to the bridge with the \(15\,\Omega\) galvanometer across the bridge gives a galvanometer current of about \(4.87\) mA. Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.14: Equal masses on the two springs have the same maximum momentum, so \(A_1\omega_1=A_2\omega_2\): \(A_1\sqrt{k_1/m}=A_2\sqrt{k_2/m}\Rightarrow \frac{A_1}{A_2}=\sqrt{\frac{k_2}{k_1}}\). Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.15: In a purely resistive circuit the current and voltage are in phase; in a purely inductive circuit the current lags the voltage by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\); in a purely capacitive circuit the current leads by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\). Matching each to its phase relation gives option (D).
authoredSolutions.16: When block A is given speed \(v\), the centre of mass moves at \(v/2\); in the CM frame the energy \(\frac12\mu v^{2}\) (reduced mass \(\mu=m/2\)) converts to spring PE \(\frac12 kx^{2}\), so the maximum compression is \(x=\sqrt{\frac{m}{2k}}\,v\). Hence option (A).
authoredSolutions.17: The visible (Balmer) series of atomic hydrogen arises from transitions ending at \(n=2\). Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.18: From the photoelectric equation \(\frac12 m v_1^{2}=hf_1-\phi\) and \(\frac12 m v_2^{2}=hf_2-\phi\), subtracting gives \(v_1^{2}-v_2^{2}=\frac{2h}{m}(f_1-f_2)\). Hence option (A).
authoredSolutions.19: In a purely inductive circuit \(X_L=\omega L=2\pi f L\), so halving the frequency halves the inductive reactance; the current \(I=V/X_L\) then doubles. Hence option (B).

authoredSolutions.45: In the Solvay process, ammonia is recovered by treating the \(NH_4Cl\) solution with \(Ca(OH)_2\); the by-product formed is calcium chloride, \(CaCl_2\). Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.46: (A) is the arenediazonium salt \(CH_3O\text{-}C_6H_4\text{-}N_2^+Cl^-\). On warming with ethanol it undergoes reductive deamination to anisole, the ethanol being oxidised to acetaldehyde (X = \(CH_3CHO\)) with \(HCl\) released (Y), along with \(N_2\). Hence option (A).
authoredSolutions.63: Writing the equation as \(\frac{dy}{dx}-(\tan x)y=\frac{1}{(3\sin x+\cos x+3)\cos x}\), the integrating factor is \(e^{-\int\tan x\,dx}=\cos x\). Solving gives \(y\cos x=\ln(3\sin x+\cos x+3)+C\), and applying the initial condition yields the relation in option (B). Hence option (B).
authoredSolutions.72: With \(x,y,z\) in A.P. (\(2y=x+z\)), the determinant \(\begin{vmatrix} 3 & 4\sqrt2 & x \\ 4 & 5\sqrt2 & y \\ 5 & k & z \end{vmatrix}=0\) for all such \(x,y,z\) forces the rows' coefficients to be in A.P. too, giving \(k=6\sqrt2\). Hence option (A).
authoredSolutions.74: If the angle between the two tangents from \(P\) is \(\theta\) with \(\tan\theta=\frac{12}{5}\), then \(\tan\frac{\theta}{2}=\frac{2}{3}\), and \(PA=r\cot\frac{\theta}{2}\) for the circle of radius 1 about \((1,2)\). The required quantity then evaluates to option (B). Hence option (B).
authoredSolutions.75: On \((0,\infty)\), \(f(x)=\left(2-\sin\frac1x\right)x\), so \(f'(x)=2-\sin\frac1x+\frac{\cos\frac1x}{x}\). As \(x\to0^+\) the term \(\frac{\cos(1/x)}{x}\) oscillates with unbounded amplitude, so \(f'\) changes sign infinitely often near 0 and \(f\) is not monotonic on \((0,\infty)\); the same holds on \((-\infty,0)\). Hence option (B).
